Crypto financing announcements have totaled approximately $408.55 million across nine disclosed transactions during Nov. 7–13, 2026, led by a reported $270 million commitment to the bank-backed stablecoin venture Project Faro.
Summary
Nine disclosed financings totaled $408.55 million, including bank commitments and two public token sales.
Project Faro drew approximately $270 million in reported commitments for five years of operations.
Index Industries raised $50 million in seed funding led by Lightspeed Venture Partners.
Alta secured a $47.5 million Series A, bringing its cumulative funding to $80 million.
Project Faro, Index and Alta accounted for nearly 90% of the disclosed weekly total.
The tally includes corporate funding commitments and public token sales alongside venture rounds. Four further announcements covered cumulative or undisclosed funding.
DefiLlama’s funding database provided the weekly inventory, with company announcements, investor disclosures and reporting used to check transaction details.
Project Faro leads crypto financing with $270 million commitment
Goldman Sachs, Citigroup, Santander and Deutsche Bank were among institutions committing around $270 million to a stablecoin venture , as crypto.news reported, citing Bloomberg’s Nov. 10 report.
Known as Project Faro, the proposed business would use the capital to cover five years of operating costs. The figure represents committed corporate financing, with no announcement that the full amount has been paid.
The 21-member consortium expects to establish its issuer in the United States. Its stated launch window is the first half of 2027, beginning with a dollar stablecoin intended for payments and digital asset settlement. A euro token is planned later.

Founded by former Polychain president Josh Rosenthal and Longmark CEO Brian Hardecker, the company is developing a daily U.S. home-price index and tokenization infrastructure for housing-linked investment products.
Its first planned application is USHP, issued separately by British Virgin Islands-based USHP Limited. The issuer plans an Ethereum release in 2026 and a Solana expansion in 2027.
The announcement states that the referenced securities are unregistered in the United States and cannot be offered to U.S. persons without registration or an applicable exemption.
Alta secures $47.5 million for institutional blockchain infrastructure
Alta announced a $47.5 million Series A led by Index Ventures on Nov. 10, with GV, Blackbird Ventures, Square Peg and Capital49 participating.

articles.text:
UA Little Rock: $266.5 Million Centennial Campaign Exceeds Fundraising Goal
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 1:31 AM
UA Little Rock: $266.5 Million Centennial Campaign Exceeds Fundraising Goal
The University of Arkansas at Little Rock has completed its Centennial Campaign with $266.5 million raised, surpassing its $250 million goal and setting a fundraising record for the university.
The seven-year campaign attracted 22,762 donors who made 197,887 contributions. University leaders announced the final total of $266,532,569.07 during a November 5 celebration recognizing donors, alumni and community partners.
The campaign established 211 endowments and helped increase the university’s endowment by 192%. Its investments span scholarships, student support, academic leadership, research and campus facilities.
Private support helped launch the Half-Off Scholarship, which reduced tuition costs for incoming freshmen, and the Trojan Guarantee, which covers remaining tuition for qualifying students receiving both a Pell Grant and the Arkansas Academic Challenge Scholarship.
A $7.5 million Windgate Foundation gift established the Enduring Opportunity Scholarship Program to help sustain the university’s affordability initiatives.
Academic investments included endowed directorships supporting nursing, education and engineering. The university also expanded simulation-based nursing education and developed a year-long paid teacher residency program.
Campus improvements included the revitalization of Trojan Way and renovations to 22 classrooms and laboratories. The Shellam Flake planetarium is scheduled for a soft opening in December 2026.
The fundraising effort included more than 19,000 face-to-face visits by the development team with donors and prospective supporters. Campaign co-chairs Alfred Williams and Jerry Damerow helped lead the initiative alongside university leadership and a broader campaign cabinet.
The new endowments will provide continuing support after the campaign’s conclusion, extending its effects beyond immediate construction projects and scholarship awards to future students, faculty and academic programs.
KEY QUOTES:
“Seven years ago, a $250 million campaign for UA Little Rock might have seemed out of reach. Tonight, we celebrate not just reaching that goal, but what reaching it says about who we have become.”
Christina S. Drale, Chancellor Of The University Of Arkansas At Little Rock
“Those investments have changed UA Little Rock forever. They have helped us become stronger, more innovative and better positioned to serve our students than ever before.”
Christina S. Drale, Chancellor Of The University Of Arkansas At Little Rock

articles.text:

Swiss VC Redalpine Raises $250 Million for A.I., Robotics and Biotech
Jakob Steinschaden , co-produced by AI 10. November 2026, 08:00
The redalpine team, which has closed its eighth early-stage fund at $250 million. © redalpine
Set Trending Topics as a preferred source on Google.
While many venture capital firms spend months courting investors, Redalpine was done in less than a year: The Swiss firm has closed its eighth early-stage fund, Redalpine Capital VIII (RAC VIII), at $250 million. The fund was oversubscribed and is larger than its predecessor, which closed at $200 million in 2024. Redalpine now manages more than $1.4 billion in total.
Where the Money Is Going
With RAC VIII, Redalpine plans to invest in about 20 European start-ups at the seed to Series A stage, selected from more than 5,000 companies it reviews each year. Checks range from $1 million to $15 million, and Redalpine often leads the rounds. The focus is on companies at the intersection of software and science. Half of the investment team has a background in the natural sciences or engineering, according to Redalpine.
The first three investments from the new fund:
Enact Intelligence: The Zurich robotics start-up aims to give robots a sense of touch and recently raised a $30 million pre-seed round with backing from Yann LeCun, among others.
Helical: The London start-up is building a virtual A.I. lab for drug discovery. Redalpine previously led its $10 million seed round .
Arlequin AI: The team, based in Paris, Berlin and London, is developing an A.I. architecture to protect critical systems and works with government agencies.
Sebastian Becker, a general partner, said artificial intelligence was leveling the playing field for founders around the world, giving the edge to those who best understand the science behind a product and the hardest problems.
Aviva, Flexstone and KfW as Backers
The limited partners in RAC VIII include existing and new investors, among them the British asset manager Aviva Investors, Flexstone Partners and the German development bank KfW. Redalpine was founded in Zurich in 2006, is now based in Zug and has offices in Berlin and London.
Its portfolio includes well-known names such as Mistral AI, N26 and Proxima Fusion. Redalpine led the Munich fusion start-up’s seed round, and in the summer, Proxima raised €411 million at a €2.4 billion valuation . Since 2023, Redalpine says it has sold or taken public 12 portfolio companies. They include the Swiss biotech Araris, which the Japanese drugmaker Taiho acquired for up to $1.14 billion , and, according to Redalpine, Memo Therapeutics (to Ipsen) and the A.I. security start-up Lakera (to Check Point). Companies from its previous fund, RAC VII, have raised more than $1.1 billion from investors in total.
The Competition
Redalpine is not the only firm raising fresh capital for European tech start-ups this year. In Zurich, Lakestar closed Lakestar Resilience I, a $300 million fund for defense and dual-use technologies. Headline raised $400 million for its eighth fund, which targets seed and Series A rounds in A.I., and Accel’s new European fund comes to $800 million. In Germany, Uplift Ventures launched a €100 million deep-tech fund that also invests in seed to Series A rounds.

articles.title: Model ML raises $250M to automate investment banking grunt work
articles.snippet: The startup says its agents understand the full context of deals that bankers and consultants are working on and can automatically update financial models and presentations when new developments affect their analysis.
articles.text:
In Brief
Posted:
11:32 AM PST · November 17, 2026
Image Credits: shapecharge / Getty Images
Marina Temkin
Model ML raises $250M to automate investment banking grunt work
Model ML, a London-based startup that uses AI to automate work traditionally performed by junior bankers and consultants, including building financial models, preparing pitch decks, and writing due diligence reports, has raised $250 million in Series B funding at a $1.5 billion valuation. The new round, which comes a year after its $75 million Series A round was announced, was co-led by General Atlantic and earlier backer QED Investors.
Brothers Chaz and Arnie Englander co-founded the three-year-old startup after previously co-founding two other companies, including Fat Llama, a peer-to-peer rental marketplace acquired by Swedish rival Hygglo for $41.5 million in 2022.
Model ML develops AI agents that integrate with clients’ systems, data, and tools, including Excel and PowerPoint. The startup says its agents understand the full context of deals that bankers and consultants are working on and can automatically update financial models and presentations when new developments affect their analysis.
Other startups automating the routine, repetitive tasks for investment bankers and management consultants include Hebbia and Rogo, which raised $160 million at a $2 billion valuation in April.
Anthropic and OpenAI have also built tools for financial professionals, but Model ML says it runs on open source models and that doing so allows it to operate at about 2% of the cost of frontier models while delivering faster results.

ACWA Power , SA15CGS10H12
ACWA Power stock: $226 million financing closes for Uzbek wind farm
Published on 11/16/2026 at 00:08 | Editorial responsibility: Rafael Müller, Editor-in-Chief AD HOC NEWS
ACWA Power secured long-term financing for a wind project in Uzbekistan. The milestone supports the developer's international renewable-energy expansion.
Uzbekistan project reaches financing milestone
ACWA Power secured long-term funding for the Bash II wind farm in Uzbekistan.
The project strengthens the company’s development portfolio across energy and water infrastructure.
ACWA Power is expanding projects from its Riyadh headquarters across international markets.
ACWA Power, SA15CGS10H12, Illustration mit AI erstellt.
ACWA Power has reached financial close on the Bash II wind farm in Uzbekistan's Bukhara Region, according to Oil & Gas News on Sunday, November 15. The Saudi developer secured long-term financing of 226 million US dollars, equivalent to 847.5 million Saudi riyals, from a consortium of international lenders.
Financing advances Uzbekistan project
Bash II has a planned capacity of 300 megawatts and is located in Uzbekistan's Bukhara Region. Financial close marks the transition from project development toward construction and operation, although the report did not provide a commercial start date or identify the lending consortium.
For investors, the financing milestone adds to ACWA Power's pipeline of contracted and developing energy assets. The project also underlines the role of project finance in funding large renewable-energy installations without relying solely on corporate balance-sheet capital.
International energy and water platform
ACWA Power leads energy, water and green hydrogen projects from its headquarters in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Its activities span power generation, water desalination, renewable energy and storage projects across international markets. The company works with partners, customers and communities across multiple regions, giving its portfolio exposure to infrastructure demand beyond its home market.

articles.text:

Sanofi-backed Windward Bio raises $225 million in its Nasdaq IPO as Rezera postpones its listing
Nov 13, 2026
·
6:57 PM

By MLQ.ai Newsroom · Edited by Peter Foy
·
2 min read
Key points
Windward sold 10,294,117 shares at $17 and Sanofi bought $50 million of shares and pre-funded warrants at the same price, for $225 million in expected gross proceeds [1] .
Its lead drug, WIN378, a TSLP antibody licensed from China's Kelun Biotech, is in a Phase 2/3 asthma trial with results expected next year [2] .
Rezera postponed its $200 million IPO of 16.7 million shares at $11 to $13 [3] [4] .
Windward Bio Group priced its initial public offering of 10,294,117 shares at $17 each on Nov. 12, the midpoint of its $16 to $18 range, and sold an additional $50 million of shares and pre-funded warrants to Sanofi in a concurrent private placement at the same price [1] [5] . Gross proceeds are expected to total $225 million before fees and before the underwriters' option on 1,544,117 more shares [1] . The stock began trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on Friday under the symbol WWB, and the deal is set to close on Nov. 16 [1] .
Boston-based Rezera postponed a planned $200 million IPO on the evening of Nov. 11, citing market conditions, according to IPOScoop [4] . Jefferies and TD Cowen were bookrunners on both deals, alongside Piper Sandler and UBS for Windward and Cantor Fitzgerald for Rezera [1] [3] .
Two drugs licensed from China
Windward, formed two years ago, raised $365 million of venture funding before the IPO [2] . Its lead drug, WIN378, is an ultra-long-acting injectable that blocks TSLP, the same inflammatory protein targeted by AstraZeneca and Amgen's Tezspire, and could be dosed as rarely as twice a year against Tezspire's monthly schedule [2] . Windward licensed it from Kelun Biotech, which co-developed it with Harbour BioMed [2] . The Phase 3 part of an asthma trial began in September with results expected next year, and a mid-stage COPD study started in June with data due in 2027 [2] . A second drug, WIN027, licensed from Qyuns Therapeutics, targets both TSLP and IL-13 [2] . Windward paid $70 million upfront in cash and equity for the two programs and owes up to $1.6 billion more in milestone payments [2] .
Windward is the biotech sector's 30th IPO this year, according to BioPharma Dive, which counts 2026 as the busiest year for drugmaker listings since 2021, with more than $8 billion raised [2] .
Rezera steps back
Rezera, formerly NodThera, develops oral NLRP3 inhibitors for inflammatory diseases and describes itself as Phase 3-ready [3] [4] . It had planned to sell 16.7 million shares at $11 to $13 on the Nasdaq under the symbol RZRA, and GSK had indicated interest in buying up to $25 million of the offering, about 13% of the deal [3] . Its last amended registration statement was filed with the SEC on Nov. 9 [6] . The company has not said when it might return. The postponement came in the same week that Anthropic's bankers weighed pricing its IPO above its marketed range.

articles.text:
Windward Bio Raises $225 Million In Nasdaq Debut At $1.69 Billion Market Capitalization
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 9:36 AM
Windward Bio Raises $225 Million In Nasdaq Debut At $1.69 Billion Market Capitalization
Windward Bio Group has completed its public market debut after pricing an initial public offering at $17 per share and raising $225 million in gross proceeds, including a $50 million concurrent private placement from Sanofi.
The clinical-stage biotechnology company began trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on November 13, 2026 and ended its first day with a market capitalization of approximately $1.69 billion.
Windward sold approximately 10.29 million ordinary shares in the offering.
The Basel, Switzerland-based company was founded in 2024 by serial biotechnology entrepreneur Luca Santarelli, M.D., and his team. Santarelli previously helped build VectivBio and Therachon, both of which were ultimately acquired.
Windward has raised $365 million since its formation, including a $200 million Series A in January 2025 and a $165 million crossover financing in May 2026.
Pivotal bioVenture Partners China has invested in the company through each financing round from its early formation through the public listing.
Windward is developing ultra-long-acting antibody treatments for respiratory and dermatologic diseases including asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and atopic dermatitis.
Its lead program, WIN378, is a fully human monoclonal antibody targeting thymic stromal lymphopoietin.
WIN378 is currently being evaluated in the Phase 2/3 POLARIS-1 asthma study and the Phase 2 SIRIUS COPD trial. The drug is being developed for twice-yearly dosing, compared with the once-every-four-weeks schedule of currently approved treatments in the category.
Windward reported positive interim Phase 2 data in September 2026 supporting twice-yearly dosing of WIN378 in asthma.
Its pipeline also includes WIN027, a clinical-stage bispecific antibody targeting TSLP and IL-13 that is currently in Phase 1 development.
Global rights outside Greater China and certain Asian markets to both programs were licensed from Chinese biopharmaceutical companies.
Windward plans to use IPO proceeds to support clinical development of WIN378 and WIN027, advance additional bispecific antibody programs and fund working capital and general corporate purposes.
The company expects top-line Phase 2 asthma data for WIN378 in the first half of 2027, Phase 2 COPD data in the second half of 2027 and Phase 3 asthma data in the first half of 2029.
